# utils

**In one sentence:** Small, DOM-free helpers that hold the Caption Verifier's state: the edited captions, the rendered previews, and the list of verdicts.

## Why it exists
The Caption Verifier modal (see `../caption_verify.js`) needs to remember what the user typed, which preview image belongs to which photo, and what each verdict means. Keeping that in plain functions keeps the modal class short and easy to test.

## What's inside
| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `captions.js` | Caption store, a `Map` from image path to `{ text, original }`. `createCaptionStore`, `readCaption`, `setCaption`, `isEdited` (trimmed text differs from the original), and `buildSubmitValue`, which builds the `{ items: { path: { verdict, caption, edited } } }` answer sent back to Python. |
| `previews.js` | `createPreviewStore()` keeps rendered previews and their status (`idle` / `generating` / `error`) per image path. `isPreviewStale(preview, caption)` is true when the caption was edited after that preview was rendered. |
| `verdicts.js` | The three verdicts: `correct` ("Renders correctly"), `generic` ("Renders generic") and `wrong` ("Renders wrong"), plus `DEFAULT_CAPTION_VERDICT` (`correct`) and `normalizeCaptionVerdict`, which turns any unknown value into `correct`. |

## How it works
- The modal makes one caption store from the payload items. The textarea writes into it on every keystroke.
- Previews are stored by image path, not by "the selected image", so a slow render still lands on the photo it was started for.
- On submit, `buildSubmitValue` sends every item with its verdict (default `correct`), its current caption text, and an `edited` flag. The comment says Python recomputes `edited` itself and does not trust this flag.

## Who uses it
- `../caption_verify.js`: uses all three files.
- `../components/editor.js` and `../components/strip.js`: use `verdicts.js`. `../components/preview.js`: uses `isPreviewStale`.
- Tests: `tests/ui/static/caption_verify.test.js`, which drives the whole modal.

## Good to know
- `captionVerdictLabel` in `verdicts.js` is exported but nothing imports it, so it is unused.
